command_crashed.description: An exception that no registered failure path covers ended the command; a defect. The traceback goes to stderr.

config_invalid.description: The configuration cannot be used: LOCALAPPDATA is unset or not absolute (location_invalid), or config.json cannot be read, is not UTF-8 JSON, repeats a key, has an unknown or missing member, or a value of the wrong type. The error's ref is the JSON pointer of the member.

data_external_hash_mismatch.description: acmodel check: the local copy of a data table's external dataset (dataset, the file named by its sha256 under paths.datasets) does not hash to the declared sha256; found is its sha256. path is the data file; the error's ref is /external/sha256.

data_external_missing.description: acmodel check: a data table declares an external dataset, and its local copy (dataset, the file named by its sha256 under paths.datasets) is absent or cannot be read (exception_type, raw_text). Fetching it is the data side's work; the tool only verifies. path is the data file; the error's ref is /external.

data_reference_missing.description: acmodel check: a data reference (data:<table>[<key>].<column>, a data set, or lookup) names a table no data file of the model holds, a column the table does not declare, or a key that matches no inline row or has the wrong number of parts (row). path is the file of the expression; the error's ref is the JSON pointer of the expression and position the character offset of the reference.

deps_invalid.description: The venv or a pinned package is missing, a package is not at its pin, or the interpreter (or the venv's interpreter) is not Python 3.13. setup_command is the command that creates the venv; setup never replaces a venv of another minor version.

expr_dimension_mismatch.description: An operator or function of an expression gets operands whose types do not fit: an amount of one resource with another, an amount with a time, a bare number with a time, a boolean where a number is needed or the reverse (expr/dimensions.py lists the rules). operands are the operands' types (amount:<resource>, time, count, value, none, number, bool); position is the character offset of the operator. The error's ref is the JSON pointer of the expression. acmodel run (contracts/formats.md, The run) adds path, the file, and also refuses: an expression whose type does not fit what its member expects (operator is the member, e.g. when, value, max, every, consumes, moves, general_logic, offset; operands are the expected and the found type; position is the expression's top operator); a reference whose value has no type in the language (operator reference; operands is a preference's JSON type string, array, object or null, or a column's type enum or id); a fact key declared with two dimensions (operator read); a lookup key that does not fit its key column (operator lookup); the variants of a member or the bounds of a range that do not fit each other (operator variants, interval or distribution); a threshold of a boolean (operator threshold, ref in exports.json).

expr_eval_failed.description: Evaluating an expression failed: a division by zero, clamp with its low bound above its high bound, or a value from the model (a reference, flow, lookup or set) that is not of the type the check gave it (expected is that type, or members for a set; found is the value's Python type). evaluation_unsupported (acmodel run): the expression reads what this version does not evaluate yet, and found names it: metric, count or pref (a reference of that kind), interval or distribution (an unknown of that kind), random (a random:<id> product), external_dataset (a row of an external table), when (a rule's condition); operator is reference, the function or the member. Every output that needs it is blocked. The error's ref is the JSON pointer of the expression; acmodel run adds path, the file.

expr_overflow.description: A literal, a value read or an intermediate result of an expression has a numerator or denominator of more than max_bits bits (configuration key expr.max_bits; durations count in seconds). Nothing wraps or rounds. operator is the operator or function, literal or reference. The error's ref is the JSON pointer of the expression; acmodel run adds path, the file, and blocks every output that needs it.

expr_parse_error.description: An expression does not parse (grammar in expr/syntax.py): a character outside the language, a malformed number, an unexpected token or end, an unknown reference kind, a malformed reference (or a set where a value is needed), the member key $ outside a sum or count over its set, an unknown function, a wrong number of arguments, or an argument of the wrong form. position is the character offset; token is the offending text. The error's ref is the JSON pointer of the expression; acmodel check adds path, the file that holds it.

host_gate_paused.description: The host gate holds compute; a later run or check resumes (contracts/cli.md, Host caps). One entry per reason that holds. memory_below_start: the available host memory (available_mib) is below host.memory.start_min_mib (limit_mib) before a batch, or while the gate is paused. memory_below_pause: inside a batch it fell below host.memory.pause_below_mib (limit_mib). quiet_window: the local time is inside host.quiet_windows[window]. pause_file: the file host.pause_file (path) exists. cpu_load: the host CPU load over the last window (load_milli) is above host.cpu.pause_load_milli (limit_milli). plan_above_report: the planned memory of the run (estimate_mib) is above host.memory.report_plan_above_mib (limit_mib), so the run is reported before it starts.

host_job_not_applied.description: The Job object that caps the tool's processes (CPU rate, memory per process, priority class) could not be created (CreateJobObjectW), configured (SetInformationJobObject: set_limits, set_cpu_rate), joined by the current process (AssignProcessToJobObject) or read back (verify: QueryInformationJobObject, IsProcessInJob). In verify, limit names the limit read back with another value than configured (expected, found), or membership when the current process or a child started afterwards is not in the Job. os_error is GetLastError when a call failed. Nothing computes without the Job.

host_priority_not_applied.description: The priority class of compute.priority (expected is its Windows value) is not in effect. set: SetPriorityClass returned 0 (os_error). verify: GetPriorityClass of the current process, or of a child started after the caps, reads another class (found; 0 with os_error when the call itself failed). platform_unsupported: only Windows has a real host layer, so on this platform the caps cannot be applied. Nothing computes at normal priority.

host_reading_failed.description: A reading of the host layer failed, so the gate or the check cannot decide and does not guess. memory: GlobalMemoryStatusEx. cpu_times: GetSystemTimes, or counters that did not advance consistently over a window. pause_file: checking whether host.pause_file exists failed other than by its absence (path, exception_type, raw_text). process: opening or closing a child process to verify it (OpenProcess, CloseHandle). call is the Win32 function and os_error its GetLastError.

model_file_invalid.description: An input file of the model (model, rules, data, sources, exports, state, preference defaults) is refused by its strict reader (contracts/formats.md), or (acmodel run) a state snapshot names another model: value_invalid at /model_id, expected is the model's id. The error's ref is the JSON pointer of the value (the empty pointer for the whole file); path is the file and format the reader. JSON level: unreadable, bom_present, utf8_invalid (offset), syntax_invalid (line, column), key_duplicate (the repeated key), float_literal, constant_invalid (NaN, Infinity), integer_out_of_range (beyond +-(2^53-1)), string_invalid (a lone surrogate). Shape: type_invalid (expected types), member_unknown, member_missing, member_conflict (two of members that exclude each other; expected lists them), value_invalid (expected values), id_invalid (the id grammar). One error per problem; literal is the offending text.

model_id_duplicate.description: acmodel check: an id is declared twice in one namespace. model: entities, periods, rules and unknowns share one; table: data tables; row: the keys of one table's rows (id joins the key parts with commas); source: sources.json; engine: model.json engines; threshold (acmodel run): the thresholds of exports.json. path and the error's ref are the second declaration, first_path and first_ref the first, which references resolve to.

rule_conflict.description: acmodel check: two active rules of the same kind hold the same subject and slot (contracts/formats.md lists the slot of each kind; slot is cap_kind for cap and per for limit), and neither supersedes the other. id is the later rule, conflicts_with the earlier; the error's ref is the later rule.

rule_cycle.description: acmodel check: rules and unknowns that depend on each other in a loop (via reference: through their expressions, flow functions and gate requirements) or that supersede each other in a loop (via supersedes). members are the loop's nodes, sorted (rule:<id>, unknown:<id> or unknown:<id>.<member>); path and the error's ref point at the first member's first link into the loop.

rule_pending_unbounded.description: acmodel check: a pending rule names no unknown (no_unknown; ref is its status), or only unknowns without a range form (unknown_unbounded; ref is its status), or a rule or unknown references an unknown without a range form in an expression (unknown_unbounded; ref is the expression, position the reference). acmodel run: an expression reads a pending data row, which cannot name an unknown (no_unknown; id is <table>[<key parts joined with commas>]; path and ref are the expression's). Without a range, everything that needs it is blocked.

rule_pref_misplaced.description: acmodel check: an expression reads a preference (pref:<key>) outside a gate rule or an objective's terms (#424 design D-2). id and kind are the rule or unknown (kind unknown) that holds it; the error's ref is the JSON pointer of the expression and position the character offset of the reference.

rule_provenance_missing.description: acmodel check: a rule, an unknown, a data row or a data table has an empty provenance list, or a data row has none and its table gives none. id is the entry's id (a row's key parts joined with commas, a table's id); the error's ref is the empty list, or the row.

rule_reference_missing.description: acmodel check: a reference to a declaration of the model does not resolve to one of the expected kinds (an entity kind, entity, rule, rule.<kind>, unknown, unknown_member, metric, engine, source or param): nothing has that id, it is of another kind (found), or it is a superseded rule (superseded_by), which is never read. The error's ref is the JSON pointer of the referring member or expression, and position the reference's character offset in an expression. acmodel run (contracts/formats.md, The run) adds: pref, a preference key (pref:<key>, a gate's prefs) that the preference defaults do not hold; rule.derive, rule.cap, rule.limit, a rule: reference to a rule without a value; resource, store, a cap's subject; rule.flow, a cost or yield (target the activity) or max_single_income (target the cap) with no flow amount behind it; rule.derive and rule.derive.live, the from of a threshold in exports.json, which needs live in the fact_offset form.

rule_status_invalid.description: acmodel check: a status outside its closed set: confirmed, pending or provisional for rules and data rows; pending or provisional for unknowns. id is the entry's id; the error's ref is the status.

ruling_overrides_general_logic.description: A note of acmodel run (data.notes, never an error): a derive's value differs from its general_logic, the #425 general rule's value. The value stands, by its provenance (a ruling, say); the difference is reported, never hidden. value and general_logic are their distinct exact values, sorted (one each without variants). path and the note's ref are the general_logic expression.

state_entity_missing.description: acmodel run: an expression reads an entity of the account state that the state snapshot does not hold: its class (entity_class, absent from the state's entities), the entity (entity:<class>[<id>]), or the entity's attribute. Every output that needs it is blocked; the others are computed. path and the error's ref are the expression, position the reference.

state_reading_missing.description: acmodel run: a reading of the account state is needed and the state snapshot does not hold it: the fact key fact (read:<fact>, a cap's reading, or the reading of an entity that amount:<id> or stock:<id> reads), or entity, a resource or store that declares no reading. There is no fallback to a constant. Every output that needs it is blocked; the others are computed. path and the error's ref are the expression (or a cap's reading), position the reference.

state_reference_missing.description: acmodel check: a reference into the account state does not resolve: a fact key (read:<fact>, live.fact, live.reference_fact) that no entity or active cap of the model declares as its reading, an entity class (entity:<class>) that is not an entity_class entity, or an attribute (target) that its class (entity_class) does not declare. The error's ref is the JSON pointer of the referring member or expression, and position the reference's character offset in an expression.

usage_invalid.description: The command line names no command, an unknown command, or an argument the command does not take, or it lacks an argument the command needs (argument is the argument's name). The usage text goes to stderr.

venv_failed.description: Work on the venv failed. inspect: the configured path exists but holds no venv (no readable pyvenv.cfg version); it is refused, never replaced. create: python -m venv failed. install: pip failed. dispatch: the venv's Python could not be started, or a re-dispatched child still did not run in the venv (found is its prefix).
